recommendations.title: Say it back, slower
recommendations.what_to_do: When they babble, say the sound back to them and wait. Leave a gap long enough to feel awkward.
recommendations.why_this: The gap is the lesson. It teaches that talking has turns in it, long before words arrive.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Pauses and looks at you after making a sound

recommendations.title: Name what they are staring at
recommendations.what_to_do: Follow their eyes and say the thing out loud. “Bus.” “Rain.” One word, no sentence.
recommendations.why_this: Words stick to the thing they are already interested in, not the thing you chose.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Looks from the object to you and back

recommendations.title: One song at every nappy change
recommendations.what_to_do: Pick a song and sing only that one at changes for a fortnight.
recommendations.why_this: Repetition in a fixed slot is how the earliest patterns get laid down.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Stills or kicks when the song starts

recommendations.title: Ask for it in words, once
recommendations.what_to_do: When they point, name it and wait two beats before handing it over. Once, not every time.
recommendations.why_this: One prompt teaches. Ten prompts turn asking into a chore they will avoid.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Says or attempts a word instead of pointing

recommendations.title: Two-word Tuesdays
recommendations.what_to_do: For one day, stretch their one word into two. “Cup.” → “Big cup.”
recommendations.why_this: You model the next step without asking them to perform it.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Copies the second word back

recommendations.title: Tell dad what happened
recommendations.what_to_do: At the end of the day, ask them to tell someone else one thing that happened.
recommendations.why_this: Retelling to a person who was not there is much harder than answering you, and it is where narrative starts.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Includes one detail unprompted

recommendations.title: The three-part story
recommendations.what_to_do: Ask about their day using only: what happened first, then what, then what.
recommendations.why_this: Three slots are enough scaffolding to hang a story on and few enough to finish.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Puts events in the right order

recommendations.title: Explain it to the toy
recommendations.what_to_do: Ask them to explain a rule or a game to a teddy while you listen.
recommendations.why_this: Explaining exposes what they actually understand, without it feeling like a test.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Corrects themselves halfway through

recommendations.title: The question they ask back
recommendations.what_to_do: Answer one of their questions properly, then ask one back and wait.
recommendations.why_this: Conversation is a rally. Most adult-child talk is serve after serve.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Asks a follow-up question of their own

recommendations.title: Best bit, worst bit
recommendations.what_to_do: Over tea, each of you says one good and one hard thing about the day. You go first.
recommendations.why_this: Going first makes the hard half safe to answer honestly.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Offers a hard thing without being asked

recommendations.title: Read the page, then close it
recommendations.what_to_do: After a page, close the book and ask what happened. Then open it and check together.
recommendations.why_this: Checking together turns being wrong into something ordinary.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Remembers detail rather than the gist

recommendations.title: Give the directions
recommendations.what_to_do: Let them direct you somewhere familiar — the shop, the park — while you do exactly as told.
recommendations.why_this: Instructions have to be precise to work, and doing exactly as told shows them where they were vague.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Corrects an instruction when it goes wrong

recommendations.title: Disagree on purpose
recommendations.what_to_do: Pick something harmless and take the other side. Make them argue you round.
recommendations.why_this: Holding a position under gentle pressure is a different skill from talking.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Gives a reason rather than repeating themselves

recommendations.title: Explain it to someone younger
recommendations.what_to_do: Have them teach a younger child or a grandparent something they know well.
recommendations.why_this: Teaching forces them to find simpler words for what they know.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Changes their explanation when it does not land

recommendations.title: The phone call
recommendations.what_to_do: Have them ring to book, order or ask something, with you nearby but silent.
recommendations.why_this: Speaking to a stranger without a face to read is harder and more useful than it looks.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Handles an unexpected answer

recommendations.title: Two minutes, no notes
recommendations.what_to_do: Ask them to talk for two minutes about anything they care about. Time it.
recommendations.why_this: Two minutes is long enough to run out of the obvious and start thinking.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Keeps going past the first thirty seconds

recommendations.title: Say the difficult thing
recommendations.what_to_do: Help them write, then say, one thing they have been avoiding saying to someone.
recommendations.why_this: The hard conversations of secondary school are rehearsable, and rehearsal is most of it.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Says it without softening it into nothing

recommendations.title: Summarise the argument
recommendations.what_to_do: After a documentary or an article, ask them to give both sides fairly before saying what they think.
recommendations.why_this: Steelmanning is the skill underneath every essay they will write for the next decade.
recommendations.you_might_notice: States the side they disagree with fairly

recommendations.title: Floor time, no seat
recommendations.what_to_do: Ten minutes flat on the floor next to them, nothing propping them up.
recommendations.why_this: Everything from rolling to walking is built from time spent on the floor working against gravity.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Pushes up, rolls, or shifts weight

recommendations.title: Reach just past
recommendations.what_to_do: Put the toy slightly further than they can reach, then leave it there.
recommendations.why_this: The stretch is the point. Handing it over ends the exercise.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Shifts position rather than giving up

recommendations.title: Bare feet outside
recommendations.what_to_do: Ten minutes on grass, sand, or a path with nothing on their feet.
recommendations.why_this: Balance is built from what the feet feel, and shoes remove most of it.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Adjusts footing on the uneven bit

recommendations.title: The kerb walk
recommendations.what_to_do: Walk a low wall or kerb holding one hand, then try none.
recommendations.why_this: One hand is the whole exercise. Two hands does the balancing for them.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Puts arms out to correct themselves

recommendations.title: Carry the heavy thing
recommendations.what_to_do: Give them something genuinely heavy for their size to carry a short distance.
recommendations.why_this: Load teaches the body where it is, which is most of coordination at this age.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Adjusts grip or stance without being told

recommendations.title: Posting and pinching
recommendations.what_to_do: Anything that goes into a slot: coins in a tin, pegs on a bowl, pasta in a bottle.
recommendations.why_this: The pincer grip is what a pencil is waiting for.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Uses thumb and finger rather than a fist

recommendations.title: Ten minutes of block play after tea
recommendations.what_to_do: Build a tower together, then let them knock it down. Build it again.
recommendations.why_this: The knocking down is the point. Rebuilding after it falls only works if failing is fun.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Tries again after it falls

recommendations.title: Puddle route
recommendations.what_to_do: Walk somewhere with the specific job of getting round, over or through every puddle.
recommendations.why_this: A route with obstacles does more for balance than a flat walk twice as long.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Chooses their own way over an obstacle

recommendations.title: Scissors and a magazine
recommendations.what_to_do: Give them safety scissors and something they are allowed to destroy.
recommendations.why_this: Cutting is two hands doing different jobs at once, which is harder than it looks.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Holds the paper with the other hand

recommendations.title: Twenty throws
recommendations.what_to_do: Twenty throws and catches, counting out loud, no competition.
recommendations.why_this: Counting keeps it going long enough to improve rather than stopping at the first miss.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Adjusts their aim after a miss

recommendations.title: The bike without stabilisers
recommendations.what_to_do: One session on grass, on a slight slope, with the pedals off.
recommendations.why_this: Balance first, pedalling second. The pedals are the easy half.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Lifts both feet for a moment

recommendations.title: Handwriting, five lines only
recommendations.what_to_do: Five lines of something they want to write. Stop at five even if it is going well.
recommendations.why_this: Stopping while it is still going well is what stops writing becoming a fight.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Grip stays relaxed to the end

recommendations.title: The route they choose
recommendations.what_to_do: Let them plan and lead a walk or ride of a set length.
recommendations.why_this: Ownership is what turns exercise from something done to them into something they do.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Adjusts the plan when it is not working

recommendations.title: One skill, ten minutes, three days
recommendations.what_to_do: Pick one thing — keepy-uppies, a cartwheel — and do ten minutes on three separate days.
recommendations.why_this: Spacing beats cramming for anything physical, and three days is enough to feel it.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Beats their own previous count

recommendations.title: Cook something with a knife
recommendations.what_to_do: A real task with a real blade, supervised, start to finish.
recommendations.why_this: Fine motor control with genuine stakes concentrates the mind like nothing else.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Slows down at the difficult part

recommendations.title: Something they are bad at
recommendations.what_to_do: Try a sport or activity neither of you has done before, together.
recommendations.why_this: At this age being visibly bad at something in front of a parent is rarer and more valuable than getting better at what they already do.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Stays past the first embarrassing bit

recommendations.title: Walk it instead
recommendations.what_to_do: One journey a week done on foot or by bike that would normally be a car.
recommendations.why_this: Habit beats intensity for everything that matters at this age.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Suggests the walk themselves

recommendations.title: Carry the weight
recommendations.what_to_do: Give them the heavy bag, the shopping, the younger sibling's kit.
recommendations.why_this: Being genuinely useful physically is how a growing body learns what it can do.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Takes it without being asked twice

recommendations.title: Name it before the nap
recommendations.what_to_do: As they get tired, say what you see. “You're tired. It's hard.”
recommendations.why_this: Feelings get named by an adult for a long time before a child can name them.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Settles slightly when you say it

recommendations.title: Stay for the crying
recommendations.what_to_do: When they cry, stay close and quiet rather than fixing or distracting.
recommendations.why_this: Being accompanied through a feeling is the whole of early self-regulation.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Calms faster with you there than alone

recommendations.title: The same goodbye
recommendations.what_to_do: Use the exact same words and actions every time you leave the room.
recommendations.why_this: Predictability is what makes separation survivable at this age.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Protests less over a fortnight

recommendations.title: Say it, do not ask it
recommendations.what_to_do: “You're cross because it fell.” Not “are you cross?”
recommendations.why_this: At two they cannot yet answer the question. They can hear the label.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Repeats the feeling word back

recommendations.title: Wait for the sand timer
recommendations.what_to_do: Use a two-minute timer for turns. Sit with them while it runs.
recommendations.why_this: Waiting is a physical skill first, an emotional one second.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Waits without needing to be held

recommendations.title: Let the small no stand
recommendations.what_to_do: Pick one small thing today where the answer is no, and do not soften it.
recommendations.why_this: A no that survives a protest is what makes the world feel solid.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Recovers within a few minutes

recommendations.title: Name the feeling before the nap
recommendations.what_to_do: Say what you think they are feeling, out loud, before rest time.
recommendations.why_this: Naming it lowers it. The word does most of the work.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Uses a feeling word themselves

recommendations.title: The rewind
recommendations.what_to_do: After a wobble, retell it calmly together: what happened, what it felt like, what helped.
recommendations.why_this: Retelling turns a flood into a story with a shape, which is what makes it manageable next time.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Adds their own detail to the story

recommendations.title: Lose the game
recommendations.what_to_do: Play something you will win. Let them lose and stay with them through it.
recommendations.why_this: Losing safely, with company, is the only way to practise it.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Wants to play again after losing

recommendations.title: Where do you feel it?
recommendations.what_to_do: When they are upset, ask where in their body they feel it.
recommendations.why_this: The body is easier to describe than the feeling, and it is a way in.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Points to a real place

recommendations.title: The waiting jar
recommendations.what_to_do: Something they want goes in a jar for a week before they get it.
recommendations.why_this: Waiting practised on something pleasant is waiting they can draw on when it is hard.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Checks the jar without demanding it

recommendations.title: Angry on paper
recommendations.what_to_do: Give them paper and let them scribble the feeling out, no words needed.
recommendations.why_this: An outlet that does not need language works when language has gone.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Reaches for the paper unprompted

recommendations.title: What would you tell a friend?
recommendations.what_to_do: When they are hard on themselves, ask what they would say to a friend in that spot.
recommendations.why_this: They are almost always kinder to an imagined friend, and they notice the gap.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Softens their own verdict

recommendations.title: The evening handover
recommendations.what_to_do: Ten minutes where they talk and you only ask questions. No advice.
recommendations.why_this: Advice ends the conversation. Questions keep it open.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Volunteers something you did not know

recommendations.title: Name it before it lands
recommendations.what_to_do: Before something you know is hard — a test, a party — name the feeling in advance.
recommendations.why_this: Anticipating a feeling takes most of its power away.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Names the feeling first next time

recommendations.title: Say the hard thing badly
recommendations.what_to_do: Tell them a time you handled a feeling badly, without a moral at the end.
recommendations.why_this: A parent who was once out of their depth is more use than one who was always fine.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Tells you something of their own

recommendations.title: Twenty minutes before answering
recommendations.what_to_do: When something lands hard, agree not to reply to it for twenty minutes.
recommendations.why_this: The gap between feeling and acting is the whole skill, and it is trainable.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Waits before replying to a message

recommendations.title: The thing they cannot fix
recommendations.what_to_do: Talk about something genuinely unfixable, and do not fix it.
recommendations.why_this: Tolerating an unsolved problem is the adult version of this skill.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Stays in the conversation

recommendations.title: Let them hold the spoon
recommendations.what_to_do: Give them a spoon of their own during feeding, even though it will not work.
recommendations.why_this: Doing it badly for months is how doing it well starts.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Gets the spoon to their mouth loaded or not

recommendations.title: Pause before helping
recommendations.what_to_do: Count to five before stepping in on anything they are struggling with.
recommendations.why_this: Most of what a baby learns happens in the seconds an adult usually fills.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Solves it themselves within the five

recommendations.title: One job at bathtime
recommendations.what_to_do: Give them one part of the routine that is theirs — the flannel, the plug.
recommendations.why_this: A job that is genuinely theirs is different from being allowed to help.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Reaches for their job unprompted

recommendations.title: Coat on the floor flip
recommendations.what_to_do: Teach the flip: coat on the floor, hood at their feet, arms in, flip over the head.
recommendations.why_this: One method taught properly beats being dressed quickly forty times.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Attempts the flip without prompting

recommendations.title: Their own cup, poured
recommendations.what_to_do: A small jug and their own cup at meals. Expect spills for a fortnight.
recommendations.why_this: The spills are the fortnight-long cost of a skill they keep for life.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Pours without over-filling

recommendations.title: Put it back yourself
recommendations.what_to_do: One thing a day goes back where it came from, by them, before the next thing starts.
recommendations.why_this: One consistent thing beats a tidy-up battle over everything.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Puts it back without a reminder

recommendations.title: Dressed before breakfast
recommendations.what_to_do: Clothes out the night before, dressing before food, no clock.
recommendations.why_this: Removing the rush is what makes the skill possible. The rush is usually ours, not theirs.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Finishes without help

recommendations.title: Ask a grown-up for it
recommendations.what_to_do: At the shop or cafe, they ask for the thing themselves while you stand back.
recommendations.why_this: Speaking to a stranger with you nearby is the safest version of a hard skill.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Asks without you prompting the words

recommendations.title: The forgotten thing
recommendations.what_to_do: When they forget something for nursery, let them notice rather than catching it.
recommendations.why_this: The consequence teaches what the reminder cannot.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Checks their own bag next time

recommendations.title: Pack your own bag
recommendations.what_to_do: They pack for school from a list they can read, and you do not check it.
recommendations.why_this: Checking it removes the whole lesson.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Notices a missing item themselves

recommendations.title: Make one meal a week
recommendations.what_to_do: The same simple meal every week until it is theirs.
recommendations.why_this: Repetition on one dish gets to competence faster than variety.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Does a step without being told

recommendations.title: Money that runs out
recommendations.what_to_do: A small fixed amount for the week, spent how they choose, not topped up.
recommendations.why_this: Running out on Wednesday is the lesson. Topping up deletes it.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Changes what they buy the next week

recommendations.title: The errand alone
recommendations.what_to_do: One short trip they do without you — the corner shop, a neighbour's door.
recommendations.why_this: Independence needs actual distance from a parent, in a dose you both survive.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Handles something unexpected on the way

recommendations.title: Their own alarm
recommendations.what_to_do: They set it, they get up to it, and you do not act as a backup.
recommendations.why_this: Being late once is a cheaper teacher than being woken for a year.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Gets up without a second prompt

recommendations.title: Fix the broken thing
recommendations.what_to_do: Something small breaks — let them try to mend it before it is replaced.
recommendations.why_this: Repair is a habit of mind, and it starts with being allowed to try.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Works out what is wrong before asking

recommendations.title: Manage the week
recommendations.what_to_do: Hand over one recurring responsibility entirely — the washing, the bins, a sibling's lift.
recommendations.why_this: Owning something end to end is different from being asked each time.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Does it without being reminded twice

recommendations.title: The journey they plan
recommendations.what_to_do: They plan a route with a change on it, and lead it.
recommendations.why_this: Secondary school arrives with journeys attached. Practise before it counts.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Recovers when a connection is missed

recommendations.title: Their own money, their own mistake
recommendations.what_to_do: A larger sum, a longer period, and a purchase you privately think is a mistake.
recommendations.why_this: A mistake at twelve costs pennies. The same lesson at twenty costs real money.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Reflects on it without being lectured

recommendations.title: Face to face, no screen
recommendations.what_to_do: Ten minutes of nothing but looking at each other and copying faces.
recommendations.why_this: Faces are the first thing they study and the foundation of reading people.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Copies an expression back

recommendations.title: Peekaboo, properly
recommendations.what_to_do: Play until they get bored rather than until you do.
recommendations.why_this: Peekaboo is a lesson that people come back, run hundreds of times.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Starts the game themselves

recommendations.title: Watch other children
recommendations.what_to_do: Sit somewhere other children are playing and just watch together.
recommendations.why_this: Watching is what comes before joining, and it is not idleness.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Tracks another child across the space

recommendations.title: Play alongside, not with
recommendations.what_to_do: Arrange to be near another child with similar toys and no requirement to share.
recommendations.why_this: Parallel play is the real developmental stage here. Forcing sharing skips it.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Glances at what the other child is doing

recommendations.title: One turn each
recommendations.what_to_do: A simple game with strict turns and you keeping the rhythm.
recommendations.why_this: Turn-taking is the mechanical form of every relationship skill that follows.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Waits for their turn once

recommendations.title: Say what they wanted
recommendations.what_to_do: When two children clash, say out loud what each of them wanted.
recommendations.why_this: They cannot yet see the other side. Hearing it named is the start.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Looks at the other child while you say it

recommendations.title: Invite one child, not three
recommendations.what_to_do: One friend, at home, for a short visit.
recommendations.why_this: One friend is a friendship. Three is a crowd to survive.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Suggests a game to the other child

recommendations.title: How do you think they felt?
recommendations.what_to_do: After a story or a clash, ask about the other person's side.
recommendations.why_this: Perspective-taking is askable at this age and it was not at two.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Offers a plausible feeling for someone else

recommendations.title: Give it away
recommendations.what_to_do: Let them choose something of theirs to give to someone who would like it.
recommendations.why_this: Chosen generosity feels different from enforced sharing, and it sticks.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Chooses something they actually like

recommendations.title: The fallout, replayed
recommendations.what_to_do: After a falling-out, act it out with toys, both parts.
recommendations.why_this: Playing both parts is the only way to feel the other side at this age.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Plays the other child fairly

recommendations.title: Write to someone
recommendations.what_to_do: A card or a drawing for someone they do not see often.
recommendations.why_this: Keeping a relationship warm across distance is a skill, and it starts here.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Adds something personal to it

recommendations.title: Include the one on their own
recommendations.what_to_do: Talk about who was on their own at playtime, and what could be done.
recommendations.why_this: Noticing is the skill. Acting comes after, and only if noticing is practised.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Names someone unprompted

recommendations.title: The disagreement, repaired
recommendations.what_to_do: After a row with a friend, help them plan the repair rather than the argument.
recommendations.why_this: Repair is the skill that keeps friendships. Winning is not.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Goes back to the friend themselves

recommendations.title: Host it themselves
recommendations.what_to_do: They plan and run an activity for a friend, start to finish.
recommendations.why_this: Hosting means putting someone else's enjoyment first for two hours.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Checks whether the friend is enjoying it

recommendations.title: Say no to a friend
recommendations.what_to_do: Rehearse turning down something a friend wants, without falling out.
recommendations.why_this: This is the year that mattering to friends starts to override mattering to you.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Says no without a long excuse

recommendations.title: The group chat, read together
recommendations.what_to_do: With permission, look at a group chat together and talk about tone.
recommendations.why_this: Text has no face on it, and most of the trouble at this age is tone misread.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Spots where something could be read two ways

recommendations.title: Someone outside the group
recommendations.what_to_do: Encourage one friendship outside the main group — a cousin, a club, a neighbour.
recommendations.why_this: A single group is fragile. A second circle is what makes falling out survivable.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Keeps up the second friendship unprompted

recommendations.title: Stand next to someone
recommendations.what_to_do: Talk about the difference between defending someone loudly and simply standing next to them.
recommendations.why_this: The quieter version is the one they can actually do at twelve.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Describes a time they did it

recommendations.title: The same book, again
recommendations.what_to_do: Read the one they keep choosing, as many times as they choose it.
recommendations.why_this: Repetition is how the words come loose from the page.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Turns the page before you do

recommendations.title: Point at the words
recommendations.what_to_do: Run a finger under the words as you read them.
recommendations.why_this: It teaches that the marks are the story, not the pictures.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Watches your finger rather than the picture

recommendations.title: Board books they can wreck
recommendations.what_to_do: Let them chew, drop and carry a book about.
recommendations.why_this: A book that is a possession gets read more than one that is precious.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Brings a book to you

recommendations.title: Leave the last word
recommendations.what_to_do: Read a rhyme they know and stop before the rhyming word.
recommendations.why_this: Filling the gap is reading before reading.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Fills in the word

recommendations.title: Marks that mean something
recommendations.what_to_do: Let them scribble and then ask what it says. Write their answer underneath.
recommendations.why_this: Meaning first, letters later. It is the right way round.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Tells you what their marks say

recommendations.title: The shopping list
recommendations.what_to_do: They add a scribble to the list and then find that item in the shop.
recommendations.why_this: Writing that does a job is worth ten worksheets.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Looks at their mark to remember

recommendations.title: One story with a rhyme in it
recommendations.what_to_do: Any book where they can finish the line for you.
recommendations.why_this: Rhyme is how the ear learns to break words into sounds, which is where reading starts.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Finishes the line before you get there

recommendations.title: Their name, everywhere
recommendations.what_to_do: Write their name on things and let them copy it.
recommendations.why_this: Their own name is the most motivating word in the language.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Gets the first letter right consistently

recommendations.title: Sound out one word a day
recommendations.what_to_do: One word, broken into sounds, then blended back.
recommendations.why_this: One word done properly beats twenty rushed.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Blends the sounds without help

recommendations.title: Read to the dog
recommendations.what_to_do: They read aloud to a pet, a toy, or a very patient sibling.
recommendations.why_this: An audience that cannot correct them is where fluency grows.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Reads on past a mistake

recommendations.title: You read one, I read one
recommendations.what_to_do: Alternate pages so the book still moves at a satisfying pace.
recommendations.why_this: The story staying enjoyable is what keeps them coming back.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Asks to read more than their share

recommendations.title: Write the actual letter
recommendations.what_to_do: A real letter to a real person who will really reply.
recommendations.why_this: A reply arriving is worth more than any amount of practice.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Wants to write back

recommendations.title: Twenty minutes, their choice
recommendations.what_to_do: Twenty minutes reading anything they choose, including comics and match reports.
recommendations.why_this: Volume beats quality at this age, and choice drives volume.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Carries on past twenty minutes

recommendations.title: The audiobook and the book
recommendations.what_to_do: Same story, both formats, at the same time if they like.
recommendations.why_this: Hearing fluent reading while following the text is one of the strongest supports there is.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Follows the text while listening

recommendations.title: Write the instructions
recommendations.what_to_do: They write instructions for something, and you follow them exactly and literally.
recommendations.why_this: Following them literally shows precisely where the writing was unclear.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Rewrites the vague step

recommendations.title: The book you disagree about
recommendations.what_to_do: Read the same thing and argue about it.
recommendations.why_this: Reading becomes a social act, which is what keeps it alive through secondary.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Holds a view about a character

recommendations.title: Plan before writing
recommendations.what_to_do: Five bullet points before any piece of writing longer than a page.
recommendations.why_this: The planning habit is what separates a struggling writer from a competent one at secondary.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Plans without being told

recommendations.title: Edit, do not rewrite
recommendations.what_to_do: Take one paragraph they have written and improve it together, line by line.
recommendations.why_this: Editing is a distinct skill and almost nobody teaches it.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Cuts a word of their own

recommendations.title: Count the stairs
recommendations.what_to_do: Count out loud on the stairs, every time, the same way.
recommendations.why_this: Number words arrive as a song long before they mean quantity.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Joins in with a number word

recommendations.title: Two of everything
recommendations.skill: How many, and which is more
recommendations.what_to_do: Hand things over in twos and say “two” as you do it.
recommendations.why_this: Small quantities are recognised before they are counted.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Holds a hand out for the second one

recommendations.title: The posting box
recommendations.what_to_do: Anything that goes in a hole: shapes, coins, socks in a drawer.
recommendations.why_this: Sorting is the root of every pattern that follows.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Tries a different hole after a miss

recommendations.title: One for you, one for me
recommendations.what_to_do: Share things out one at a time, saying it aloud.
recommendations.why_this: One-to-one matching is the idea underneath counting.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Gives one each rather than a handful

recommendations.title: Big one, little one
recommendations.skill: How many, and which is more
recommendations.what_to_do: Sort the washing, the shoes, the spoons into big and little.
recommendations.why_this: Comparison comes before measurement.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Sorts correctly without help

recommendations.title: Stripes and spots
recommendations.what_to_do: Point out repeating patterns on clothes, tiles, railings.
recommendations.why_this: Spotting a repeat is the beginning of algebra, however unlikely that sounds.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Points out a pattern themselves

recommendations.title: Set the table
recommendations.what_to_do: They work out how many plates, cups and forks are needed.
recommendations.why_this: A real problem with a real answer beats a worksheet.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Counts the people first

recommendations.title: Which pile is more?
recommendations.skill: How many, and which is more
recommendations.what_to_do: Two piles of something, and they say which is more, then check by counting.
recommendations.why_this: Estimating then checking is what builds number sense rather than number reciting.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Estimates before counting

recommendations.title: Make the pattern carry on
recommendations.what_to_do: Start a pattern with buttons or blocks and let them continue it.
recommendations.why_this: Continuing a pattern is harder than copying one, and more useful.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Extends it correctly by two more

recommendations.title: Pay with the coins
recommendations.what_to_do: They hand over real money and work out the change.
recommendations.why_this: Money is the only place most children meet arithmetic with consequences.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Works out the change before it is given

recommendations.title: Double it
recommendations.skill: How many, and which is more
recommendations.what_to_do: Halve or double a recipe together and work out the new amounts.
recommendations.why_this: Multiplication in a kitchen sticks better than multiplication on paper.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Doubles one ingredient unaided

recommendations.title: Guess then measure
recommendations.what_to_do: Guess a length or a weight, then measure it.
recommendations.why_this: Being wrong then measuring is what calibrates estimation.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Second guess is closer than the first

recommendations.title: The budget is theirs
recommendations.what_to_do: Give them a budget for a real thing and let them work it out.
recommendations.why_this: Constraints make arithmetic matter.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Adjusts the plan to fit the money

recommendations.title: Read the table
recommendations.skill: How many, and which is more
recommendations.what_to_do: A timetable, a league table, a nutrition label — find three things in it.
recommendations.why_this: Reading data is a distinct skill from calculating with it.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Finds an answer without your help

recommendations.title: Why does that work?
recommendations.what_to_do: When they get an answer, ask how they know rather than whether it is right.
recommendations.why_this: Explaining a method is what turns a trick into understanding.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Describes their method in words

recommendations.title: Is that number honest?
recommendations.what_to_do: Take a statistic from an advert or an article and pull it apart together.
recommendations.why_this: Numbers used to persuade are the ones they will meet most, and least often question.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Asks what the number is compared with

recommendations.title: Plan the cost of it
recommendations.skill: How many, and which is more
recommendations.what_to_do: Something they want — work out the true total including everything.
recommendations.why_this: Total cost of ownership is a genuinely adult idea and this is the age for it.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Includes a cost you had not mentioned

recommendations.title: The pattern in the data
recommendations.what_to_do: Track something for a fortnight — sleep, weather, screen time — then look for a pattern.
recommendations.why_this: Collecting your own data changes how you read everybody else's.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Notices something you had not

recommendations.title: Out in the weather
recommendations.what_to_do: Go outside in whatever it is doing and name it.
recommendations.why_this: Weather is the first natural system a child meets.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Reacts differently to rain than to sun

recommendations.title: The same walk
recommendations.what_to_do: Walk the same short route regularly and point at the same things.
recommendations.why_this: Familiarity is what makes noticing change possible.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Looks for a landmark before you point

recommendations.title: What does it do?
recommendations.what_to_do: Let them work taps, switches, lids and catches.
recommendations.why_this: Cause and effect is learned by hand.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Repeats an action to see it happen again

recommendations.title: Dig somewhere
recommendations.what_to_do: Give them a patch of soil and something to dig with.
recommendations.why_this: Soil holds more discoverable things per minute than any toy.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Notices something living

recommendations.title: Who does that job?
recommendations.what_to_do: Name the people you see working — the driver, the postie, the builder.
recommendations.why_this: Communities are made of roles, and roles are nameable at two.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Names a job unprompted

recommendations.title: Then and now photos
recommendations.what_to_do: Look at photos of them as a baby and talk about what has changed.
recommendations.why_this: Personal history is the first history anyone understands.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Says something has changed

recommendations.title: Grow one thing
recommendations.what_to_do: Plant something fast — cress, beans — and check it daily.
recommendations.why_this: Daily checking is what makes slow change visible.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Reports a change without being asked

recommendations.title: Where does it come from?
recommendations.what_to_do: Pick one food and trace it back as far as you both can.
recommendations.why_this: Everything comes from somewhere, and that is a genuinely new idea at four.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Asks about another food

recommendations.title: Somebody else's celebration
recommendations.what_to_do: Learn about a festival that is not yours, from someone who keeps it if you can.
recommendations.why_this: Difference met early is difference that never becomes strange.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Asks a question about it

recommendations.title: The map of here
recommendations.what_to_do: Draw a map of your street or your route to school together.
recommendations.why_this: Turning space into a drawing is a substantial mental leap.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Gets the order of landmarks right

recommendations.title: Take it apart
recommendations.what_to_do: Something broken and safe, dismantled with a screwdriver.
recommendations.why_this: Inside is where the interest is, and most children never get to look.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Works out what a part is for

recommendations.title: When you were little
recommendations.what_to_do: Ask a grandparent or older relative what was different.
recommendations.why_this: History from a person beats history from a book at this age.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Asks a follow-up question

recommendations.title: Follow one story
recommendations.what_to_do: Pick a news story and follow it for a fortnight.
recommendations.why_this: Following something over time shows that events have causes and consequences.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Predicts what happens next

recommendations.title: The local walk with a question
recommendations.what_to_do: Walk somewhere with one question to answer — why is that there, who built it.
recommendations.why_this: A question turns a walk into an investigation.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Finds evidence rather than guessing

recommendations.title: Where does the rubbish go?
recommendations.what_to_do: Trace one waste stream from your bin to wherever it ends up.
recommendations.why_this: Systems become real when you follow one all the way.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Changes a habit as a result

recommendations.title: Two sources, one story
recommendations.what_to_do: Read two accounts of the same event and find where they differ.
recommendations.why_this: Source comparison is the whole of critical thinking, in miniature.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Spots a difference in emphasis

recommendations.title: How does that get paid for?
recommendations.what_to_do: Pick something public — a park, a bus, a hospital — and work out who pays.
recommendations.why_this: Civic understanding starts with the money.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Asks about something else public

recommendations.title: The thing they would change
recommendations.what_to_do: Ask what they would change locally, then find out who actually decides it.
recommendations.why_this: Discovering that a real person decides is what makes agency feel possible.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Names the actual decision-maker

recommendations.title: Bang something
recommendations.what_to_do: Wooden spoons, pans, boxes. Join in rather than supervising.
recommendations.why_this: Rhythm is made with the whole body before it is made with an instrument.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Repeats a rhythm you made

recommendations.title: One pot of paint
recommendations.what_to_do: One colour, big paper, hands allowed.
recommendations.why_this: One colour removes the choosing and leaves the doing.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Makes a deliberate mark rather than a smear

recommendations.title: Sing the ordinary
recommendations.what_to_do: Sing what you are doing rather than saying it.
recommendations.why_this: Melody carries language further into memory than speech does.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Vocalises along with you

recommendations.title: The box is a boat
recommendations.what_to_do: Give them a big box and say nothing about what it is.
recommendations.why_this: Saying nothing is the active ingredient.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Decides what it is themselves

recommendations.title: Playdough with no cutters
recommendations.what_to_do: Dough and hands only, no shape cutters.
recommendations.why_this: Cutters make outcomes. Hands make decisions.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Makes something they name

recommendations.title: Dress up from the drawer
recommendations.what_to_do: Ordinary clothes, not costumes, for pretending.
recommendations.why_this: Ordinary clothes require more imagination than a costume that has already decided.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Stays in character for a minute

recommendations.title: Draw the story you just read
recommendations.what_to_do: After a book, draw the bit they liked.
recommendations.why_this: Moving a story between forms is what deepens it.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Chooses a moment rather than the cover

recommendations.title: Junk model
recommendations.what_to_do: A box of packaging, tape, and no instructions.
recommendations.why_this: Open materials produce ideas; kits produce assembly.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Changes the plan halfway through

recommendations.title: Make up the verse
recommendations.what_to_do: Take a song they know and change the words together.
recommendations.why_this: Altering something familiar is easier and bolder than inventing from nothing.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Offers a line of their own

recommendations.title: The comic strip
recommendations.what_to_do: Six boxes, one story, words optional.
recommendations.why_this: Six boxes force a beginning, a middle and an end.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Uses the boxes to show time passing

recommendations.title: Build it for someone
recommendations.what_to_do: Make something for a specific person, to be given.
recommendations.why_this: An audience changes every decision, for the better.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Adjusts it for who it is for

recommendations.title: Copy a proper artist
recommendations.what_to_do: Pick a real painting and copy it badly on purpose.
recommendations.why_this: Copying teaches technique without the pressure of originality.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Notices a choice the artist made

recommendations.title: Finish the bad first draft
recommendations.what_to_do: Make something quickly and badly all the way to the end before improving any of it.
recommendations.why_this: Finishing is the skill. Perfecting the opening is the trap.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Gets to the end before editing

recommendations.title: Learn one riff
recommendations.what_to_do: One short piece of music, learned properly, on anything.
recommendations.why_this: One thing played well beats six things half-learned.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Practises without being asked

recommendations.title: Their own rules
recommendations.what_to_do: They invent a game with written rules, and you play it exactly as written.
recommendations.why_this: Playing it exactly as written exposes every hole, which is the fun of it.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Rewrites a rule after playing

recommendations.title: Make something in public
recommendations.what_to_do: Post, perform, or show something to more than the family.
recommendations.why_this: Sharing work is a separate skill from making it, and harder.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Shares it despite being nervous

recommendations.title: Study something they love
recommendations.what_to_do: Take apart a song, a game or a film they already love and ask why it works.
recommendations.why_this: Analysis of something loved does not kill the love; analysis of something set does.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Names a technique the maker used

recommendations.title: The long project
recommendations.what_to_do: One thing that takes more than one sitting, kept where they can see it.
recommendations.why_this: Returning to unfinished work is the habit that makes anything substantial possible.
recommendations.you_might_notice: Comes back to it a second time
